newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia to boost internal coffee price.
newsitem.headline: Colombia to boost internal coffee price.

text.p: Colombia will raise its internal coffee price as early as next week in a bid to bring it closer into line with world prices, Finance Minister Jose Antonio Ocampo said.
The internal price was raised 12 percent to 248,125 pesos per 125-kg load on January 31, but the increase fell short of growers' expectations given the recent run-up in prices in New York and London.

Instead of setting a new price for a prolonged period of time, Ocampo said the government and National Coffee Growers' Federation had decided to introduce a "sliding scale" price formula to track the ups and downs of the world market in a timely fashion.
He did not elaborate, but said the pricing formula, likely to be introduced Monday, would "allow the internal price to depend on the evolution of external prices.
"It will be a sort of sliding scale like the one that existed between 1994 and 1995," he said.
Colombian excelso fetched up to $1.70 per pound in New York in July 1995 when the sliding scale formula for internal prices was in effect.

The formula was eliminated later in the year, however, when world market prices began trending sharply downward and the state-run National Coffee Fund, which buys all Colombian coffee, established artificial support prices.

Gabriel Arango Londono, a former head of the National Coffee Exporters' Association, warned Thursday that low internal prices had led a growing number of producers to smuggle their coffee into Ecuador where it can be sold at a substantial premium.
